nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the generation $F_{n+1}$ is the union, over all intervals $[a/b, c/d] \in F_n$, of the two mediant halves $[a/b, (a + c)/(b + d)]$ and $[(a + c)/(b + d), c/d]$, where each interval $[x/y, z/w]$ is stored as the quadruple $(x, y, z, w)$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the Stern-Brocot generations

nodes.summary: The $n$-th Stern-Brocot generation $F_n$ is a finite set of intervals $[a/b, c/d]$, each stored as the quadruple $(a, b, c, d)$ of natural numbers. It is defined by $F_0 = \{[0/1, 1/1]\}$, and $F_{n+1}$ is obtained by replacing each $[a/b, c/d] \in F_n$ with its two mediant halves $[a/b, (a + c)/(b + d)]$ and $[(a + c)/(b + d), c/d]$.

Then there is a natural number $n \ge 1$ with $1/(n + 1) \le a/b$ and $c/d \le 1/n$, that is, $[a/b, c/d] \subseteq [1/(n + 1), 1/n]$.
